title: Cohere and Aleph Alpha sign $20B merger, dual-HQ in Toronto and Berlin
subtitle: The transatlantic combination pitches sovereign enterprise AI as an alternative to the US hyperscaler stack for regulated European and Canadian buyers.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Canadian AI lab Cohere and German AI lab Aleph Alpha signed a definitive merger agreement on September 16, 2026, valuing the combined company at roughly $20 billion. The unified firm will operate under the Cohere brand with dual headquarters in Toronto and Berlin; Aleph Alpha's Heidelberg office continues as an AI research center. Aidan Gomez stays CEO, Aleph Alpha co-CEO Ilhan Scheer becomes COO, and combined headcount will pass 1,000 across both continents. The deal is subject to final regulatory approvals and is expected to close later in 2026.

The real story is data sovereignty as a go-to-market wedge. Both companies have been building for enterprise and government buyers who cannot legally or operationally run their inference on US hyperscaler infrastructure — regulated banks, European ministries, Canadian public sector, defense primes. Alone, neither firm had enough scale to be a serious alternative to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. Combined, with a credible physical presence in both jurisdictions and headcount past a thousand, they have a story that a French bank or a Bundesbank contractor can actually sign a contract on.

This lands into a September that has already seen the EU AI Office publish its first frontier-model audit deadlines, Anthropic–OpenAI–Google talks about a joint safety standards body, and Ant Group's KYA agent-identity push with Visa and Mastercard. Sovereignty, jurisdiction, and interoperability are the strategic axes on which the next round of enterprise AI competition will be fought — and none of them is raw model IQ. The winners will be the vendors who can produce a compliance package as thick as their technical spec sheet.

Takeaway for learners: pay attention to who a model provider's contracts are with, not just whose benchmarks it tops. In enterprise AI, "US-based only" is a disqualifier for a growing list of regulated buyers, and a merger like Cohere–Aleph Alpha is one of the few ways a non-hyperscaler can credibly serve them. Career-wise, "sovereign AI" specialist — someone fluent in the intersection of model deployment, data residency law, and procurement — is a niche that pays well right now and will pay better in three years.
